testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When do front wheel brakes work?
questions.correctAnswerText: Under all conditions.
questions.explanation: Front wheel brakes work well in any road condition. You are unlikely to skid with front wheel brakes, even on ice.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leak rate for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the maximum leak rate is 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leak rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during an applied leakage test?
questions.correctAnswerText: 3 psi in one minute.
questions.explanation: A single vehicle with air brakes should not leak more than 3 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test. Know the safe leak rate for your specific vehicle.

questions.question: What must all air tanks have?
questions.correctAnswerText: A drain valve.
questions.explanation: All air brake tanks must have a drain valve. This valve drains water and oil that build up in the tanks. Drain valves can be manual or automatic.

questions.question: What should you do if the low pressure warning signal comes on while driving?

options.text: Leave the road and park safely as soon as you can.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the road and park safely as soon as you can.
questions.explanation: When the low pressure warning signal comes on, safely leave the road and park as soon as possible. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: What does the service brake system do?

options.text: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
Applies and releases the parking brakes.
Applies and releases the emergency brake.
Applies and releases the axle brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies and releases the brakes when you press the brake pedal while driving.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate parts: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The service brake system applies and releases the brakes when you press the pedal during normal driving.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.correctAnswerText: An air compressor.
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor breaks, neither system will work properly.

questions.question: What type of air brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dual air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems controlled by one set of controls. Each system operates brakes on different axles.

questions.question: How is water and compressor oil removed from an air storage tank?

options.text: The water and oil are siphoned out.
Open the drain valve to remove the water and oil.
Water and oil are removed automatically when brakes are used.
A sponge is used to soak up the water and oil.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the drain valve to remove the water and oil.
questions.explanation: Open the drain valve to remove water and oil from air storage tanks. This buildup damages the brakes if left in the system. Manually operated tanks must be drained daily.

questions.question: What happens when the S-cam turns after the brake pedal is pressed?

options.text: The S-cam presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
The S-cam tightens the brake drum onto the axle.
The S-cam presses the brake lining against the wheel.
The S-cam releases air from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The S-cam presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When the S-cam turns, it presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system have?
questions.correctAnswerText: The number varies.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks.

questions.question: What happens if brake pads rub against brake drums and create too much heat?

options.text: The brakes will become extra sensitive.
The air compressor will turn on to cool the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may stop working.
questions.explanation: Brakes heat up when used. If they get too hot, they become less effective and may stop working. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, how do you apply the parking brake?

options.text: By using a diamond-shaped yellow knob.
By using a round red knob.
By using a square green knob.
By using a black round knob.

questions.correctAnswerText: By using a diamond-shaped yellow knob.
questions.explanation: In a newer vehicle with air brakes, the parking brake uses a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of air in the braking system.
The pressure of air coming from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: The application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Controls how quickly air leaves the air storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of the air entering the air storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of the air leaving the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning light. It is usually red and may have a buzzer sound with it.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes in one minute?
questions.correctAnswerText: 2 psi
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a single vehicle with air brakes, air leakage should not exceed 2 psi in one minute. If it leaks faster, the vehicle should not be driven and needs repairs.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, the air pressure pushes out the rod and moves the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slack adjuster.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air enters the brake chambers. The air pressure pushes out the rods and moves slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: What should you do when you need to make an emergency stop?

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Stop in a way that keeps your vehicle in a straight line.
Stop in a way that turns your vehicle.
Expect your vehicle to slow down more quickly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop in a way that keeps your vehicle in a straight line.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Keep your vehicle traveling in a straight line while still being able to turn if needed.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake every time you park your vehicle with air brakes.

questions.question: Why should you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed from the tanks
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed from the tanks
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and oil. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with a dual brake system, what should you do first?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up so fuel reaches the engine
Wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems
Start driving right after the vehicle starts
Pump the pedal 20 times to build pressure, then drive

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, let the air compressor build up to at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Mechanical
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time. Emergency brakes in an air brake system must use mechanical force to stay engaged.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times
Push in the brake control knob

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob
questions.explanation: In vehicles with air brakes, a knob controls the parking brake. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes. Push the knob in to release them.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: They allow rain water to enter the tanks
They remove water and oil from the tanks
They must stay open while driving

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the tanks
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and oil. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.
